question: Trade winds that cross the equator and enter the Indian peninsula in _______ direction bring monsoons to India.
solution:
The correct answer is **"south-west".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A seasonal shift in wind direction is called a **monsoon.**
 
• Monsoons are reasons for **heavy rainfall. **
 
• The Indian **monsoon** is the most **prominent** monsoon in the world.
 
• The direction in which the **monsoon** blows is from land towards the Sea in the **winters** and from Sea towards land in the **summers. **
 
• The winds of monsoon blow from cold to warm climates. 
 
• The motive in the back of this phenomenon is that bloodless air fills a greater area than heated air.
 
• The low-stress place draws southeast change winds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Due to the **Coriolis** force, these trade winds turn right towards the low-pressure regions in India after crossing the **equator** and begin blowing withinside the **southwestern** direction.
 
• Thereafter those exchange winds input the peninsular part of India because of the southwest monsoon.
 
• Winters in India are dry and hot. 
 
• The monsoon winds carry moisture from the **northeast.**
 
• Most of India lies between the equator and the **tropic of cancer,** so the Indian land receives direct get right of entry to the sun’s rays.
 
• The monsoon in summer enters the Indian subcontinent from the **southwest** direction. 
 
• These winds convey moisture from the** Indian Ocean.**
 
• This brings heavy rainfall between the months of **June** to **September.**
 
• The **southeast** exchange winds emerge as the **southwest monsoon** due to the fact those exchange winds go the equator and start blowing in the **southwest** direction under the influence of the **Coriolis** force.
